name: promiscuous-cache
bug: arp-add drops the owns-target? guard: the body becomes (Bound sha) unconditionally, so the <protocol type, sender protocol address, sender hardware address> triplet is added whether or not the receiver owns ar$tpa.

name: merge-after-opcode
bug: arp-merge guards the merge on the opcode: (if (= op Req) (Bound sha) (Bound key-hw)), so an existing entry is updated only from a REQUEST and a received REPLY leaves the table unchanged.
scope_note: The registered change names both the target test and the opcode test. arp-merge's signature carries no owns-target? parameter, so only the opcode half is writable at this site; the target-test half is not expressed.

name: old-address-wins
bug: arp-merge returns (Bound key-hw): the existing entry keeps its stored hardware address instead of being superseded by ar$sha.

name: reply-to-reply
bug: arp-emission drops the opcode match and returns (Unicast sha) for every opcode inside the guard, so a received REPLY provokes a packet.

name: reply-ignores-tpa
bug: arp-add dispatches on the opcode and the Rep arm returns (Bound sha) without the owns-target? test, so processing a REPLY takes the add branch without the ar$tpa ownership test while REQUEST keeps it. This is the formal shadow of R3.

name: unicast-request
bug: arp-request-emit returns (Unicast 0) on the table miss instead of Broadcast, so the generated request goes to a single hardware address rather than to all stations on the cable.

name: reply-broadcast
bug: arp-emission's Req arm returns Broadcast instead of (Unicast sha), so the reply is broadcast rather than sent to the hardware address now held in the target hardware address field.

name: reply-fields-swapped
bug: arp-reply-spa returns spa instead of tpa, so the reply keeps the requester's protocol address in the sender field and carries no mapping for the replying station.

name: discard-suppressed
bug: arp-emission drops the (and supports? speaks?) conjunct from its guard, so a failed hardware-type or protocol test continues to the emission branch instead of ending processing and discarding the packet.
scope_note: Written at the emission locus, which carries A46. The table-side discards A47 and A49 sit on arp-frame and are deliberately not touched: one change per mutant.

name: tha-sensitive-receive
bug: arp-merge returns (Bound tha), so the receive step's table effect depends on ar$tha, a field the request form leaves a don't-care.

name: merge-key-substituted
bug: arp-add stores (Bound tha) rather than (Bound sha) under the <ar$pro, ar$spa> key, so the table is updated from the target hardware field instead of the sender hardware field.

name: hln-constant-wrong
bug: arp-request-hln returns LenOther instead of Six, so a generated Ethernet request carries a value other than 6 in ar$hln.

name: op-constant-swap
bug: arp-request-op returns Rep and arp-reply-op returns Req: the REQUEST and REPLY code points are exchanged in generation and in the reply.
scope_note: Two bodies change because the registered operator is itself a swap of one pair of constants across its two sites. It is one mutation, not two.

name: reply-drops-parameters
bug: arp-request-pln returns the constant Six instead of pln-of-hrd-pro, so the protocol-address length is not carried through from the determined length of the hardware/protocol pair.
scope_note: Partial against the registered wording, and the shortfall is stated rather than absorbed. The registered change is that THE REPLY fails to carry ar$hrd, ar$pro, ar$hln, ar$pln through unchanged. The implemented tree has no arp-reply-hrd, arp-reply-pro, arp-reply-hln or arp-reply-pln function, so the reply-side half of the registered change has no site and is not exercised by this entry. The mutation is written instead at arp-request-pln, the carrier of registered target row A76, so the entry does put field-preservation pressure on a registered target; it puts none on the reply side. Registered target A66 sits on arp-request-hrd and is not touched, so A66 is not expected to be among the refuting clauses.

name: vector-reply-mismatch
bug: Registered change: instantiated at the worked example's field values (RFC 826 lines 382-401), the constructed reply differs from the example's stated reply in ar$tha.
reason: Unwritable in the implemented tree. Row A90 is Vectored, not Encoded, and no clause in the 42-clause :source surface instantiates the worked example at any concrete field values, so no contract can refute a perturbation of it. Mutating arp-reply-tha instead would be refuted by A83, a row this entry does not target, and would report the vector as instrumented when it is not: that is the mutation-lands-somewhere-else failure, not a kill. The entry is retained and stays in the 15-mutant denominator per the closed taxonomy (prereg S5.3 #15 anticipates this outcome explicitly).
scorer_note: Having no file, this entry is invisible to score826.py's m-*.ast.json glob. It must be re-added from taxonomy.json when the matrix is assembled, or the mutant denominator reads 14 instead of the registered 15.

name: good-twin-unsolicited-reply-merges
bug: Correct variant, must stay SAFE. arp-merge dispatches on the opcode and every arm returns (Bound sha), making explicit that a REPLY merges into an existing entry exactly as a REQUEST does. RFC 826 lines 209-213 and 227-234 require this merge and lines 441-447 rely on it for recovery. A kill would mean a contract imported a check RFC 826 never specifies, most likely the frame-header check Stage B excludes as X7. This is the entry that catches a contract set which has quietly proved a better protocol than the one from 1982.

name: good-twin-tha-arbitrary
bug: Correct variant, must stay SAFE. arp-merge reads ar$tha syntactically, (if (= tha 0) (Bound sha) (Bound sha)), while the result stays invariant in it. Line 389 marks ar$tha a don't-care in the request form, so a body may mention the field as long as the table effect does not depend on it. A kill would mean a contract forbids the mention rather than the dependence.

name: good-twin-optional-checks-omitted
bug: Correct variant, must stay SAFE. Both optional length checks return true unconditionally: a receiver that performs neither check. RFC 826 lines 205 and 208 say optionally, and A48/A50 are non-rejection lemmas, so returning true satisfies them. A kill would mean a contract made an optional check mandatory.

name: good-twin-multi-owner-target
bug: Correct variant, must stay SAFE. arp-reply-spa returns (if (= spa tpa) spa tpa), which is tpa on both branches, since the then-branch is reached only when spa equals tpa: a station owning several protocol addresses replies with the matched ar$tpa as its ar$spa. This is the reading fixed as MD3 and supported by the example at lines 393-401. It also tests that the verifier reasons under the branch guard rather than matching syntax.

name: good-twin-structural-variant
bug: Correct variant, must stay SAFE. arp-emission's opcode dispatch is written as an if chain, (if (= op Req) (Unicast sha) Silent), where the implemented body uses a three-arm match whose Rep and OpOther arms are both Silent. Behaviour is identical. A kill would mean a contract fixes syntax rather than behaviour.
